rules.cwe_name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
rules.description: Finds uses of symmetric cryptography algorithms that are weak, obsolete, or otherwise unaccepted. The key lengths allowed are 128, 192, and 256 bits. These are all the key lengths supported by AES, so any application of AES is considered acceptable.

rules.cwe_name: Incorrect Behavior Order: Early Validation
rules.description: A Unicode transformation is using a remote user-controlled data. The transformation is a Unicode normalization using the algorithms "NFC" or "NFKC". In all cases, the security measures implemented or the logical validation performed to escape any injection characters, to validate using regex pattern

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection')
rules.description: Untrusted CR or LF characters are not neutralized before use in line-delimited protocol metadata.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
rules.description: Writing user input directly to a web page allows for a cross-site scripting vulnerability.

rules.cwe_name: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')
rules.description: URL redirection based on unvalidated user input may cause redirection to malicious web sites.

rules.cwe_name: Observable Timing Discrepancy
rules.description: When checking a Hash over a message, a constant-time algorithm should be used. Otherwise, an attacker may be able to forge a valid Hash for an arbitrary message by running a timing attack if they can send to the validation procedure. A successful attack can result in authentication bypass.

rules.cwe_name: Direct Request ('Forced Browsing')
rules.description: A restricted route, URL, script, or file can be requested directly without required authorization.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
rules.description: Using externally controlled strings in a command line may allow a malicious user to change the meaning of the command.

rules.cwe_name: Generation of Predictable Numbers or Identifiers
rules.description: Tokens used for sensitive tasks, such as, password recovery, and email confirmation, should not use predictable values.

rules.cwe_name: Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag
rules.description: Cookies without the `HttpOnly` attribute set can be accessed by JS scripts, making them more vulnerable to XSS attacks.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Output Used by a Downstream Component ('Injection')
rules.description: Using user-controlled data to create a template can lead to remote code execution or cross site scripting.

rules.cwe_name: Security Issue (CWE-730)
rules.description: User input should not be used in regular expressions without first being escaped, otherwise a malicious user may be able to inject an expression that could require exponential time on certain inputs.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File
rules.description: From user-controlled data saved in CSV files, it is easy to attempt information disclosure or other malicious activities when automated by spreadsheet software

rules.cwe_name: Use of Less Trusted Source
rules.description: A remote endpoint identifier is read from an HTTP header. Attackers can modify the value of the identifier to forge the client ip.
